A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoD and are readable, including all figures, tables, equations and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression benchmarks, scaling experiments, training ablations, distillation results and perceptual-supervision experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds downstream comparisons, sensitivity analyses, human ratings and semantic evaluation results.

M1.justification: Appendix B substantially revises one-step CoD: its objective adds patch-GAN and codebook-commitment terms, higher-bitrate adaptation uses staged LoRA and joint fine-tuning, and inference removes redundant AdaLN-Zero modules. Appendix F also specifies weighted one-step and multi-step losses on every post-training sample instead of subset sampling. The main foundation architecture remains stable.

E1.justification: Training still uses ImageNet-21K, OpenImages and SA-1B; image-compression evaluation still uses Kodak, CLIC2020 and Div2K. The additional human and semantic scores evaluate retained Kodak reconstructions rather than introducing a new image domain or compression task.

E2.justification: The external codec baselines are retained. Comparator membership changes locally: the one-step comparison retains OSCAR, OneDC and StableCodec but omits the standalone multi-step CoD reference shown in v1 Figure 14. v3 Figure 16 additionally compares directly fine-tuned multi-step CoD against other downstream approaches.

E3.justification: Distillation increases from 50K total steps and 5K generator updates to 100K and 10K. The X-prediction comparison changes from 256×256 at 0.0156 bpp to 512×512 at 0.0039 bpp. Figure 4 replaces FID with LPIPS. New protocols include higher-bitrate fine-tuning and Kodak evaluation using 20 human raters, semantic similarities and ten VQA questions per image.

E4.justification: v3 adds comparisons of downstream adaptation strategies, separates prediction-target effects from the JiT backbone choice, tests X-prediction within DiffC, and analyzes post-training loss-weight sensitivity (Figures 16–18). The original unified-training and auxiliary-loss ablation is retained, moving from Table 4 to Table 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or statistical significance tests. The new mean opinion scores are point estimates; no uncertainty reporting accompanies them.

E6.justification: v3 replaces and extends one-step and perceptual-supervision results, adds downstream and sensitivity curves, and reports 25.2 ms one-step processing and a 4.2 human rating. Table 1's fine-tuned MS-ILLM row changes from 21.10/0.402/0.255/80.1 to 21.08/0.376/0.248/80.92 for PSNR/LPIPS/DISTS/FID. Revised training and evaluation settings prevent interpreting all replacements as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 revises the mathematical definition of the one-step objective in Equation 10 and introduces an explicit weighted post-training objective. It also specifies the clamped X-to-velocity conversion used to explain downstream failures. The existing rectified-flow and DMD derivations remain; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a compression-oriented diffusion foundation model, inexpensive reproducible training, strong ultra-low-bitrate performance and favorable pixel-space distortion–perception trade-offs. The revised appendix substantially develops supporting applications without redefining these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the earlier favorable X-prediction conclusion by explaining its likelihood-estimation problems and degraded DiffC results. New discussion connects poor higher-bitrate multi-step fine-tuning to score-norm bias and explains downstream speed–quality trade-offs. The appendix now claims real-time one-step operation, although the conclusion retains the earlier general real-time limitation.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v3 reports release and supplies a repository link. New details specify adaptation stages, LoRA rank, learning rates and inference simplification. Table 3 corrects aggregate training cost from 116 to 464 A100 GPU-hours for the retained four-GPU schedule, while the redesigned complexity table includes conditioning in overall totals.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to LoRA and Xu's analysis of score-norm bias, using them to support adaptation and interpret downstream failures. The main related-work discussion and positioning against existing compression methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. v3 adds a change log and appendix summary, divides Appendix B into numbered subsections, inserts a downstream-analysis section and renumbers subsequent appendices. Author-footnote and wording edits are limited; much of the expanded prose documents scientific additions.

P2.justification: Figure 4 changes its plotted metric and axis, and the one-step comparison is redrawn over a wider bitrate range. The appendix adds perceptual-supervision, downstream, prediction-target and sensitivity plots, expands qualitative examples, redesigns the complexity table and adds a human/semantic-results table. Several original displays are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the foundation-model argument by extending v1's limited one-step and single-rate perceptual-supervision demonstrations into specified multi-rate applications with measured fast inference. New architectural controls and downstream failure analyses clarify when the proposed choices help or hurt. Corrected resource accounting and code-release information improve reproducibility. The stale real-time limitation and limited user-study reporting remain weaknesses, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
